description: We are harmonizing NASA FIRMS MODIS (1 km) and VIIRS (375 m) active fire hotspot detections using Python geospatial clustering and Fire Radiative Power (FRP) normalization to deliver a unified wildfire monitoring pipeline
summary: I developed a Python-based algorithm and an interactive dashboard to harmonize legacy MODIS and modern VIIRS satellite wildfire datasets. By successfully reducing Mean Absolute Error (MAE) by 28.8%, this project creates a unified, accurate fire tracking record, empowering scientists and responders to analyze historical patterns alongside real-time data.
details:
​What it does and how it works:

My project, "Multi-Sensor Wildfire Radiometric Harmonization," bridges the gap between legacy and modern satellite sensors to create a unified, highly accurate active fire tracking system. By mathematically harmonizing MODIS and VIIRS (J1/J2) datasets, the project successfully reduces the Mean Absolute Error (MAE) between the sensors by 28.8%, seamlessly aligning their radiometric signatures.

​Benefits and intended impact:

For over two decades, fire records have been split across different sensors that cannot be directly compared. This project eliminates that data discontinuity. The intended impact is to provide emergency responders, land managers, and climate scientists with a consistent, reliable tool to examine historical fire patterns alongside real-time data, enabling better early warnings and critical period anticipation.

​Tools and technologies used:

I developed this project using Python for data processing, analysis, and algorithm development. To make the data accessible, I built a live, interactive global hotspot dashboard using web mapping libraries (Folium/Leaflet). The entire project, including a detailed presentation deck, is version-controlled and hosted on GitHub/GitHub Pages.

​Creativity and factors considered:

As a solo participant, I focused on the practical, real-world challenge of data integration. Instead of simply overlaying raw datasets on a map, the creativity lies in the underlying algorithmic harmonization—solving the mathematical discrepancies between different satellite generations to create one continuous, trustworthy climate record.
